title: Rhetorical Synthesis, Part 1: The Method and Two Questions

beats.say: Rhetorical synthesis questions show a list of research notes, and then state a goal. You pick the sentence that best uses the notes to reach that goal.
The goal might be to emphasize something, to explain, to compare, or to introduce a topic to people who don't know it.
Here's the surprise. Every choice is accurate to the notes. Only one choice does what the goal asks.
Step one. Read the goal in the question first, before the notes. The goal tells you which facts matter.
Step two. Turn the goal into a short checklist. For example, both items, plus their sources, plus a contrast.
beats.item: Turn the goal into a checklist

beats.say: Step three. Check each choice against the checklist, and eliminate any choice that misses a part.
Step four. Look at the notes only if two choices both seem to fit.

scenes.title: Goals and what the answer needs
rows: name it, say what it is

beats.say: To emphasize a size or amount, the sentence must include the specific number or scale.
To explain why, the sentence must include a reason, such as because, or so that.
To compare or contrast, the sentence must mention both items, and how they relate.
To show a similarity, the sentence must state something that's true of both items.
To introduce a topic to people who don't know it, the sentence must name it, and say what it's.
Easy question. The goal is to emphasize the length of a bridge. Our checklist has one item: the sentence must talk about the length.

scenes.title: The student's notes
scenes.text: The Kessler Bridge crosses the Tamar River. It opened in 1932. It is 1,850 meters long. It was the longest bridge in the region when it opened.

beats.say: These are the notes. Only the last two facts talk about length. The others are true, but they're about the river and the date.
To emphasize length, the best sentence should give the number, and stress that it was the longest.

scenes.title: Which sentence meets the goal?
scenes.question: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to emphasize the length of the bridge?

options.A: The Kessler Bridge, which crosses the Tamar River, opened in 1932.
options.B: At 1,850 meters, the Kessler Bridge was the longest bridge in the region when it opened.
options.C: The Kessler Bridge opened in 1932 and crosses the Tamar River.
options.D: In 1932, a new bridge opened over the Tamar River.

beats.say: Choice A is true, but it's about the river and the opening date. It never mentions length.
Choice C is also true, but again it gives the date and the river, and never mentions length.
Choice D gives only the date and the river. It doesn't even name the bridge, and it never mentions length.
Choice B gives the number and stresses it, by saying it was the longest in the region. The answer is B.
Medium question. The goal is to contrast two things. The checklist has three parts: both spices, their sources, and a contrast between them.

scenes.title: The student's notes
scenes.text: Saffron and turmeric are both spices used to color food yellow. Saffron comes from the dried stigmas of a crocus flower. Turmeric comes from the dried root of a plant in the ginger family. Saffron is far more expensive because each flower yields only three stigmas, which are picked by hand.

beats.say: The goal is to contrast the sources of the two spices. So we need saffron's source, turmeric's source, and a word that shows the difference.
beats.underline: dried stigmas of a crocus flower

beats.say: The facts we need are the second and the third. The first is a similarity, and the last is about price.

scenes.title: Which sentence meets the goal?
scenes.question: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to contrast the sources of the two spices?

options.A: Saffron and turmeric are both used to give food a yellow color.
options.B: Saffron is expensive because its stigmas must be picked by hand.
options.C: While saffron comes from the dried stigmas of a crocus flower, turmeric comes from the dried root of a ginger-family plant.
options.D: Turmeric, a spice made from a dried root, is a member of the ginger family.

beats.say: Choice A gives a similarity, not a contrast. It also says nothing about the sources.
Choice B mentions only saffron, and it's about price, not about the source.
Choice D mentions only turmeric. A contrast needs both items in the sentence.
Choice C names both sources, and contrasts them with the word while. It passes all three checks. The answer is C.
To recap. Read the goal first, turn it into a checklist, and check each choice against it.
All choices are true, so eliminate by the goal. In the next video, we work through a hard question and the common traps.
